missionPremise: Since P-332 (hauska-map #419, live on Property Explorer m6wqid8u7 from 2026-09-18 15:28Z) the PANEL serves a four-state ETJ determination: `present` / `absent` / `unresolved` / `conflicting`, where `conflicting` is emitted only when city limits say `incorporated` and the ETJ read says `present` (a Texas ETJ is by definition unincorporated land outside a city's limits, so the two independently derived reads disagree and the panel names both). The hauska-engine feasibility PDF still says `unresolved` for every parcel on every surface, because the engine writes the answer as a literal rather than forwarding a read: `feasibility-model.ts:209` types the field as the single-member literal, `report-model.ts:1304` assigns it, and the PDF/narrative sentences assert it. Authority: OPS-24 (the one goal: `the card, the MCP and the PDF agree`) plus the P-204 close, which files `etjStatus` as a live serve-path defect and hands the engine half to P-358; the ruling that makes it a cutover is A-215 ruling 2 in `_decisions/2026-09-18_phase0_closeout_rulings.md` (P-336 writes the ledger cells; P-358 forwards them to the PDF). The rail already EXISTS on both sides — `services/retrieval-api/src/parcel-record-rail-registry.ts:54` and `packages/engine-core/src/parcel-record/rail-keys.ts:43` both declare `etjStatus` as a scalar jurisdiction rail — it simply reads `excluded-mid-cutover` today. Premise re-read at source in this worktree at c41a1482 (not taken from the dispatch's prose): the six production sites are enumerated in writeSiteCensus below, and `etjStatus` appears in NO other non-test engine source file (case-insensitive token grep over the whole tree, node_modules excluded).
completionPredicate: For a parcel whose `etjStatus` rail serves `record`: (1) a `present` determination renders the state, naming the city and the ring, with the determination's own source/basis carried; (2) an `absent` determination renders a checked absence ("no ETJ reaches this parcel on the rings consulted"); (3) an `incorporated` city-limits reading together with an `etjStatus` reading of `present` renders `conflicting`, naming BOTH readings and BOTH sources on the page and saying which authority to confirm with — it must NOT render a clean `present` and must NOT render `unresolved`; (4) an `unresolved` state (or an unslated rail, or a refusal, or a failed fetch) keeps today's honest sentence and carries the REAL reason rather than a bare default; (5) ETJ is never derived from city limits and city limits is never derived from ETJ; (6) the same state reaches the deterministic narrative skeleton, the open-item action sentence and the narrative payload. Falsifiable here and now by revert-and-run over fixtures for the rail's four states plus an unslated rail and a failed fetch (pre-change renders `unresolved` for all six), and two locally built PDFs whose extracted text is reported in the close. The DEPLOYED half (P-336 applies its cells, the integration seat deploys, the PDF leg reads what the panel reads) is not this lane's to execute, which is why the close will declare probe.notApplicable with the exact probe named in leave_behind — the same form P-332 used, and the honest state per OPS-24 Law 1.

railCellContract.why: P-336's writer is in flight and this lane consumes its output. The reader is written to accept a bounded, enumerated set of payload shapes and to FAIL CLOSED on anything else (a declared refusal, never a guessed state). Enumerated at CP1 so the two lanes can be checked against each other rather than against prose.

acceptedValueCellShapes.shape: cell.value is one of the four state strings ("present" | "absent" | "unresolved" | "conflicting")
acceptedValueCellShapes.reading: a bare state with no basis. A bare `conflicting` carries no readings, so it is NORMALISED BACK TO RAW `present` — the only raw that can produce `conflicting`, the mirror of hauska-map's `rawEtjStatusInHand` — and the shared rule then decides: beside an `incorporated` city-limits read the report serves `conflicting` with the block composed from the composed city-limits reading + whatever the cell carried, and beside anything else it serves the coherent `present` rather than a conflict the rule cannot produce. This is what keeps the engine's five-cell (city-limits x raw) matrix equal to the panel's, so P-331's behaviour matrix can compare them cell for cell.

acceptedValueCellShapes.shape: cell.value is an object carrying `status` plus `source` and `basis` (the P-332 `EtjFactWire` shape)
acceptedValueCellShapes.reading: the determination, carried through with its optional cityKey/cityName/ringLabel/etjId/sourceCitation/coveredBy/ringsConsulted. A determination with NO basis is refused (`readEtjFact` requires source AND basis), matching P-332's `readEtjFact`: an unfounded determination is not one.

acceptedValueCellShapes.shape: cell.value is an object carrying `state: "conflicting"` plus `cityLimits` and `etj` sub-readings (the P-332 `EtjConflictWire` shape)
acceptedValueCellShapes.reading: the ledger's OWN conflict declaration; both readings and both sources are carried through verbatim, and the shared rule is not re-derived (there is nothing to derive — the ledger already declared it)

acceptedNonValueCellKinds.reading: PROMOTED to ETJ `absent` — a cell that says "verified: this point is not inside any published ETJ ring" IS the rail's answer to the ETJ question, exactly as `recordCityLimitsAnswer` promotes an `absent-verified` cityLimits cell to `unincorporated`. The cell's own `basis.finding` (or `reason`) is carried as the basis and is what the PDF prints beside it. This is the shape P-336's dispatch names for "a determination that looked and found nothing".

NOT promoted. It is a stated absence with its own reason, but it is not the checked finding "no ring reaches this point on the rings consulted", and printing that sentence on a not-applicable cell would claim a check that did not happen. Read as `unresolved` carrying the cell's own reason — fail-closed, nothing fabricated, nothing lost. DECLARED as a decision because the alternative (promoting it to `absent`) is the plausible-looking wrong answer.
`unresolved` carrying the ledger's refusal code and reason, with the existing `recordRailRefusalReason` wording so a refusal is never silent — the P-302 posture, unchanged.

designDecision.oneWriter: A single new module, `packages/engine-core/src/site-plan/etj-determination.ts`, owns the transition from (city-limits status, rail answer) to the served four-state determination + carried fact + declared conflict + reason. `report-model.ts` calls it once; the PDF and the narrative read the composed model and never re-derive. One implementation of the rule in this repo, so there is nothing for a divergence test to police (DEV_PROCESS 2.4) — and the mirror's own drift risk is against hauska-map, which is P-331's table, not a second engine writer.
designDecision.fourStates: `JurisdictionFacts.etjStatus` is widened from the single literal `"unresolved"` to `"present" | "absent" | "unresolved" | "conflicting"`, with `etjFact?`, `etjConflict?` and `etjReason?` carried beside it — the `cityLimitsLedgerAnswer` pattern the dispatch names. The widening is backward compatible: every existing assignment of the literal and every existing fixture still type-checks, and no-rail behaviour is unchanged (unresolved, with the same sentence).
designDecision.readerPlacement: The rail reader lives beside `recordCityLimitsAnswer` in `parcel-record-reader-client.ts` (`recordEtjStatusAnswer`), because that file is the ONE place a rail answer becomes an engine field and is where the P-302 three-way rule already lives. It reuses `recordRailAnswer` rather than re-deriving the kind-switch.
designDecision.conflictRule: `conflicting` is emitted ONLY for (cityLimitsStatus === incorporated AND raw ETJ === present). incorporated+absent and unincorporated+present are coherent and serve absent / present. `conflicting` arriving from the ledger is carried through with the ledger's own readings; `present` arriving beside an incorporated city-limits read is upgraded to `conflicting` by the shared rule and the conflict block is composed from the city-limits reading and the ETJ fact.
designDecision.neverDerive: If neither an etjFact status nor a recognised top-level state is in hand the state is `unresolved` and a non-empty reason is carried. No branch reads cityLimitsStatus to produce present/absent, and no branch reads ETJ to produce a city-limits status.
designDecision.absentIsACheckedFinding: `absent` is only ever reached from (a) a determination whose own status is `absent` with its basis, or (b) an `absent-verified` cell with its basis. An unreadable or absent payload can never produce it.
designDecision.narrativeContractNotWidened: The jurisdiction object is already SPREAD into the LDT narrative payload, and that payload's shape is explicitly not this lane's to widen (the client's own comment records that widening it broke the production path on 2026-09-08). The four new fields therefore ride along inside an object that is already sent; no key is added to the request's top level.
